npar.effectSizeFootnote: Positive values mean group {{p0}} ranks higher than group {{p1}}. r = |Z|/√N (Rosenthal); rank-biserial r is the net proportion of non-overlapping pairs (-1 to +1). Hodges-Lehmann is the median of all pairwise differences ({{p0}} - {{p1}}), in the variable’s own units.
npar.pairwiseFootnote: Each row tests the null hypothesis that the distributions of Sample 1 and Sample 2 are the same. Asymptotic significances (2-sided tests) are displayed. The significance level is .05; Adj. Sig. values are Bonferroni-corrected for multiple tests.

nparBinomial.noteWeightRounded: Weighted counts were rounded to the nearest integer for the exact binomial test.

nparKS.lillieforsWarning: Mean and SD were estimated from this sample. The classical Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-value is liberal (too small) in this case — install the 'nortest' R package (setup.R) for a Lilliefors-corrected p-value, available in the Normality tab.

roc.dirLargerNote: Larger values of the test result variable(s) indicate stronger evidence for a positive actual state.
roc.dirSmallerNote: Smaller values of the test result variable(s) indicate stronger evidence for a positive actual state.
roc.seMethodNoteNegexp: The standard error of the area was computed under the bi-negative exponential assumption (Hanley & McNeil 1982); the {{name}}% interval is area ± z × SE. That assumption holds only if the test scores are exponentially distributed — the Nonparametric option makes no such assumption. The significance test uses the standard error under H₀ (area = 0.5).
roc.tiesNote: The test result variable(s) {{name}} have at least one tie between the positive actual state group and the negative actual state group. Statistics may be biased.
roc.aucFootnote: a. Under the nonparametric assumption. b. Null hypothesis: true area = 0.5.
roc.aucFootnoteNegexp: a. Under the bi-negative exponential assumption. b. Null hypothesis: true area = 0.5.
roc.cutoffFootnote: The smallest cutoff value is the minimum observed test value minus 1, and the largest cutoff value is the maximum observed test value plus 1. All the other cutoff values are the averages of two consecutive ordered observed test values.

rocAnalysis.imbalanceNote: {{name}}: the positive class is under 10% of cases — consider the Precision-Recall curve alongside the ROC curve.
rocAnalysis.compareFootnote: DeLong, DeLong & Clarke-Pearson (1988) nonparametric test for paired ROC curves — every test variable compared against the same cases/state variable.
rocAnalysis.compareAucNoWeight: AUC comparison (DeLong) was requested but skipped — the 'pROC' package's DeLong test has no weighted-case support, and a case weight is currently active. Turn off weighting to use this option.
rocAnalysis.compareAucNoPackage: AUC comparison (DeLong) was requested, but the 'pROC' R package is not installed — install it from Utilities → R Packages to use this option.
rocAnalysis.seMethodNote: The standard error of the area was computed under the nonparametric assumption (the Hanley & McNeil variance with Q1 and Q2 estimated from the data — the method SPSS uses); the {{name}}% interval is area ± z × SE. The significance test uses a different standard error: the one under H₀ (area = 0.5). They are not the same value, so the interval and the p-value are read independently.
rocAnalysis.prAucFootnote: Area under the interpolated Precision-Recall curve (trapezoids over recall). Read it against the no-skill baseline, which equals the share of positive cases.
rocAnalysis.modelQualityNote: Overall Model Quality shows the lower bound of the {{name}}% confidence interval of each area. A good model has a value above 0.5; a value below 0.5 means the model does no better than random guessing.

survival.medianTitle: Means and Medians for Survival Time
survival.needsPackage: Survival analysis requires the R 'survival' package. Run setup.R.
survival.medianCiNote: The median is the smallest observed time at which the survival estimate reaches 0.5. The 95% limits come from inverting the confidence band for S(t) (Greenwood variance, log transform) at 0.5; the linear median ± 1.96 × SE(median) approximation was not used — the two can separate noticeably in a heavily censored tail.
survival.tableTruncated: The survival table was cut off at the first 5000 rows — the full table is too large for the output view.
survival.pairwiseNoAdjustNote: Pairwise comparisons are not adjusted for multiple testing: each row is a two-sample test in its own right. With k groups there are k(k-1)/2 of them, so the chance of at least one false positive is above the nominal level.
survival.noStrataForMode: No strata variable was assigned, so "for each stratum" could not be applied; the comparison was run over the whole sample.
survival.meanRestrictedNote: The mean is the RESTRICTED mean, limited to each group's own largest observed time. When that time is censored the true mean is larger, which is why an unrestricted mean is not reported.

cox.tiesEfronNote: The data has tied event times ({{name}} repeated time(s)): the partial likelihood was computed with Efron's tie correction. Tie handling is a method choice — Breslow's correction gives slightly different values for −2LL, the LR chi-square and the coefficients.
cox.stepOmnibusTitle: Omnibus Tests of Model Coefficients by Step
cox.phTestTitle: Test of the Proportional Hazards Assumption
cox.phNote: Grambsch-Therneau test: scaled Schoenfeld residuals correlated with time. A small p means that variable's hazard ratio is not constant over follow-up — the assumption the model rests on. Consider stratifying on it, or modelling a time-dependent effect.
cox.contrastNote: {{p0}}: {{p1}} contrast coding, reference category "{{p2}}". What the coefficients mean depends on the coding — a different one gives different B values from the same data.
cox.refModalNote: Curves are drawn with scale covariates held at their means and categorical ones at their most frequent category (the mean of a set of dummies is not a case that can exist).
cox.refMeanNote: Curves are drawn with the covariates held at their means.
cox.stepLRNote: Stepwise selection used the partial likelihood-ratio (LR) statistic for both entry and removal.
cox.stepWaldNote: Stepwise selection used the partial likelihood-ratio (LR) statistic for entry and the Wald statistic for removal.
cox.stepLimit: Stepwise selection reached its step limit; the model is reported as it stood at that point.
cox.noTermsEntered: No covariate met the entry criterion — the model is empty.
cox.baselineUnavailable: The baseline function table could not be computed for this model.
cox.phUnavailable: The proportional hazards test could not be computed for this model.
cox.plotUnavailable: The plots could not be computed for this model.
cox.separateNotCategorical: The variable chosen for separate lines is not a categorical covariate in this model; a single curve was drawn.
cox.epvWarn: The model has only {{p0}} events for {{p1}} coefficients. Below about 10 events per coefficient, the estimates and their confidence intervals can be biased.
cox.schoenfeldNotAligned: Schoenfeld residuals could not be matched to cases, so they were not written as new variables. The other requested variables are unaffected.

reliability.splitFootnote: Part 1: {{p0}} · Part 2: {{p1}}. The scale is split by item order; with an odd number of items the extra item goes to Part 1.
reliability.warnSplitItems: Split-half model not computed: each half needs at least two items for its own alpha, so the scale must have at least four.

glmUni.homogTitle: Levene's Test of Equality of Error Variances — {{name}}
glmUni.paramFootnote: This parameter is set to zero by this coding convention (last category taken as reference); B values are coding-dependent.

glmMulti.boxNotComputed: Box's M was not computed: fewer than two cells have a non-singular covariance matrix.
glmMulti.royFootnote: Roy's Largest Root F is an upper bound on F that yields a lower bound on the significance level.

glmRep.mvNotComputed: Multivariate tests were not computed: too few error degrees of freedom.
glmRep.mauchlyFootnote: Tests the null hypothesis that the error covariance matrix of the orthonormalized transformed dependent variables is proportional to an identity matrix.

glmRep.leveneFootnote: Based on the mean. Tests the null hypothesis that the error variance of each dependent variable is equal across groups.
glmRep.pairwiseFootnote: Based on estimated marginal means. Adjustment for multiple comparisons: {{name}}.

tree.classFootnote: Resubstitution classification (each case predicted by the fitted tree, matching SPSS Tree's own default; the tree's minCases/maxDepth stopping rules bound overfitting, unlike a pure-memorization method).

multinom.refFootnote: The reference category is the first category.

explore.noteWeightPartial: Case weights were applied to the Descriptives table only; other Explore output is unweighted.
explore.mEstimatorsFootnote: Weighting constants: Huber 1.339 · Tukey 4.685 · Hampel 1.700 / 3.400 / 8.500 · Andrews 1.340*pi. M-Estimators cannot be computed for distributions with zero spread around the median (MAD = 0). The location estimate is an iteratively reweighted least-squares (IRLS) fit; the scale is the median absolute deviation from the median, held fixed across all iterations (not the normal-consistency-corrected MAD).
explore.warnNortestMissing: The 'nortest' R package is not installed; Kolmogorov-Smirnov used the uncorrected (asymptotic) p-value. Run setup.R to enable the Lilliefors correction.
explore.warnMassMissing: M-Estimators were requested, but the MASS R package is not installed — this table was skipped.

mixed.covCiNotComputed: Confidence intervals for the covariance parameters could not be computed (the variance estimate is at its boundary).
mixed.dfNote: Denominator degrees of freedom follow nlme's containment rule, not SPSS's Satterthwaite approximation; estimates, standard errors and t values are unaffected, and p-values can differ slightly from SPSS's.

mi.needsPackage: Multiple Imputation requires the R 'mice' package. Install it from Utilities → R Packages.
mi.pooledFootnote: The pooled estimate combines the imputations by Rubin's (1987) rules; the interval uses the t distribution with df = (m−1)(1 + ū/((1+1/m)B))². The degrees of freedom fall — and the interval widens — as the fraction of missing information rises.

bayes.needsPackage: Bayesian analysis requires the R 'BayesFactor' package. Install it from Utilities → R Packages.
bayes.priorFootnote: The Bayes factor was computed with a Cauchy prior of width r = {{p1}} on the effect size ({{p0}}). The width moves the result directly: on the same data a wider prior penalises the alternative more and lowers BF₁₀. It can be changed in the analysis dialog.
bayes.mcmcNote: The posterior summary is estimated from {{p0}} Monte Carlo (MCMC) draws with random seed {{p1}}, so running the analysis again on the same data gives the same values. The Bayes factor itself does not depend on the draws.

log.notImplemented: {{command}} — recognized SPSS command, not yet supported in SAI.
log.needTwoVars: At least two variables are required.
log.ttestSyntax: T-TEST syntax: GROUPS=g(v1 v2) /VARIABLES=x  |  PAIRS=a WITH b  |  /TESTVAL=n /VARIABLES=x.
log.recodeRange: RECODE ranges (THRU / LO / HI) aren't supported yet — use exact values.
log.computeExprError: Some rows could not be computed (first error: {{error}}) — those cells were left blank.
log.useFilter: {{command}} — use Data ▸ Select Cases (or a column filter) in Data View instead.
log.splitSyntax: SPLIT FILE syntax: BY var  |  OFF.
log.selectIfSyntax: SELECT IF syntax: (variable op value) [AND variable2 op2 value2 ...] — only an AND of simple comparisons, each on a different variable, is supported (OR and repeated variables aren't).
log.selectIfApplied: SELECT IF applied: {{count}} condition(s) turned into a column filter.
log.filterOff: Filter cleared — all column filters removed.
log.ratioSyntax: RATIO STATISTICS syntax: numerator WITH denominator [BY group].
log.partialCorrSyntax: PARTIAL CORR syntax: VARIABLES=variables BY control_variables.
log.logisticSyntax: LOGISTIC REGRESSION syntax: VARIABLES=dependent WITH covariates.
log.mixedSyntax: MIXED syntax: dependent WITH covariates /RANDOM=... SUBJECT(subject_variable).
log.bayesTtestSyntax: BAYES TTEST syntax: GROUPS=g(v1 v2) /VARIABLES=x  |  PAIRS=a WITH b  |  /TESTVAL=n /VARIABLES=x  [/CRITERIA RSCALE=(WIDE|MEDIUM|ULTRAWIDE|n)].
log.bayesRegressionSyntax: BAYES REGRESSION syntax: DEPENDENT=y /METHOD=ENTER x1 x2 [/CRITERIA RSCALE=(WIDE|MEDIUM|ULTRAWIDE|n)].
log.proportionsSyntax: PROPORTIONS syntax: /ONESAMPLE var TESTVAL=p0  |  /INDEPENDENTSAMPLES var BY groupvar  |  /PAIREDSAMPLES var1 WITH var2 (PAIRED).
log.genlinSyntax: GENLIN syntax: dependent WITH predictors /MODEL predictors DISTRIBUTION=... [/REPEATED SUBJECT=subject CORRTYPE=...].
log.npartestsSyntax: NPAR TESTS syntax: at least one /subcommand is required (e.g. /CHISQUARE=variables).
log.npartestsWilcoxonSyntax: /WILCOXON syntax: list1 WITH list2  |  variable1 variable2.
log.npartestsSubNotSupported: {{command}} — this NPAR TESTS sub-test isn't in SAI yet.
log.missingValuesSyntax: MISSING VALUES syntax: variable (value, value) or (low THRU high).
log.weightScopeNote: Weighting does not apply to every analysis; those out of scope print a warning in the output.
log.splitNotApplied: Split file is not yet applied by every analysis; those out of scope print a warning in the output.
log.olapStringVar: OLAP Cubes cannot summarize the string variable {{name}}.
log.treeSyntax: TREE: a dependent variable and at least one predictor are required.
log.knnSyntax: KNN: needs one dependent variable and at least one covariate after WITH.
log.graphSyntax: GRAPH: needs a supported chart keyword and at least one variable (HISTOGRAM, SCATTERPLOT, BAR, LINE, BOXPLOT, PPLOT, QQ).
log.blockSkipped: {{command}} … {{end}} is not supported yet — block skipped, its {{count}} command(s) were not run.
log.useGraphsMenu: {{command}} (Chart Builder syntax) cannot run yet — create the chart from the Graphs menu or with the GRAPH command.
log.formatUnsupported: The {{format}} format is not supported yet (numeric F, N, E, COMMA, DOT, PCT and string A formats are).
log.formatTypeMismatch: {{name}}: the {{format}} format does not match the variable’s type.
log.declareSyntax: {{command}} syntax: new variable names and a format, e.g. STRING name (A20). or NUMERIC x (F8.2).
log.variableAttributeSyntax: Invalid {{command}} syntax — expected a variable list and a valid value.
log.deleteVariablesSyntax: DELETE VARIABLES syntax: a list of the variables to delete.
log.deleteAllVariables: DELETE VARIABLES cannot delete every variable in the dataset.
log.doRepeatUnclosed: DO REPEAT has no matching END REPEAT — nothing was run.
log.doRepeatSyntax: DO REPEAT syntax: stand-in = item list [/stand-in = item list] (variables, numbers or quoted strings) — nothing was run.
log.doRepeatLength: DO REPEAT: every item list must have the same length — nothing was run.
log.doRepeatTooMany: DO REPEAT supports at most {{max}} repetitions — nothing was run.
log.doRepeatRunning: DO REPEAT: running the block {{count}} time(s).
log.strayBlockPart: {{command}} is only valid inside its block (no matching opening command).
log.doIfUnclosed: DO IF block is not closed with END IF — the block was not run.
log.doIfUnsupported: Only COMPUTE, IF, COUNT and nested DO IF are supported inside DO IF (found {{command}}) — the block was not run.
log.doIfSyntax: DO IF / ELSE IF syntax: DO IF (logical expression).

computeInfo.title: Compute Variable
computeInfo.body: SAI computes variables with spreadsheet formulas in the Data View. Add (or pick) a column, type a formula like =weight/(height*height) in its first cell, then fill it down. The computed values are saved to the dataset. (An SPSS-style COMPUTE command line is planned.)

r.intro: A persistent R session with your dataset pre-loaded as a read-only `data` frame. Same R engine as the menus — identical code, identical output.
r.staleHint: The dataset has changed since this session started. The R console's `data` still reflects the old state — click to refresh it.

plots.title: Plots
plots.empty: No plots yet — plot() and ggplot output appears here.

console.empty: R output appears here. Type R and press Ctrl+Enter (e.g. summary(data)).

r.sees1: `data` — a copy of the current dataset (read-only).
r.sees2: The shared R library — packages you install stay available.
r.sees3: Its own working directory — you can write to your own files freely.
r.caution1: Edits in the grid / menus / SPSS syntax don't auto-refresh `data` — call sai_data().
r.caution2: Changes in R are not written to the open dataset; use sai_commit(df) to open a data frame as a new dataset.
r.caution3: Session state is hidden — restart R and re-run top-to-bottom for reproducibility.
r.caution4: A long or infinite loop can lock the session — recover with Restart.
r.deadBanner: The R session is not running.

notice.notRunning: The R session is not running. Start R first.
notice.noLongerRunning: The R session has closed. Restart it to continue.
notice.exited: The R session closed unexpectedly (exit code {{code}}). You can restart it.
notice.disabled: The R console is turned off in Preferences.
notice.rMissing: R was not found — the R runtime is not installed.
notice.winInterrupt: The command did not respond to Stop; the R session was restarted (objects in the environment were lost).
notice.viewFailed: Could not open the table view: {{detail}}
notice.committed: “{{name}}” opened as the new dataset ({{rows}} rows × {{cols}} variables). Not saved yet.
notice.commitCancelled: sai_commit cancelled — the open dataset is unchanged.
notice.plotGone: This plot is no longer in the session — only the last 20 plots are kept.
notice.debugStopped: Debugging stopped; the rest of the command was not run.
notice.reportStopped: The report is incomplete: the R session stopped.

editor.label: R script
editor.placeholder: R script — Ctrl+Enter runs the line/selection, Ctrl+Shift+Enter runs everything. Tab completes, F1 opens help.
editor.runLineHint: Runs the statement at the caret or the selection (Ctrl+Enter)

view.info: {{rows}} rows × {{cols}} columns · read-only · click a column header to sort

env.empty: No objects in the session yet.

help.empty: Press F1 on a function name, type ?function, or search above.

plotExport.title: Export plot

pkgs.installingHint: Downloading {{name}} and its dependencies — this can take a few minutes.

pkgs.installFailed: Could not install {{name}}. Check the internet connection and the package name.
pkgs.toggleHint: Ticking runs library(), unticking runs detach()

debug.title: Debugger · Browse[{{level}}]
debug.placeholder: Browse> n, s, f, c, Q or an R expression in this frame
debug.hint: Paused: type variable names to inspect them; the Environment tab shows this frame.

report.buildHint: Runs the script chunk by chunk and builds a report with code, output and plots. #' lines become text, # %% or # Title ---- lines start sections. The code runs in the current session.
report.empty: The script has no code or text for a report.
report.incomplete: The report is incomplete: the R session stopped, so the remaining chunks were not run.

r.tip1: Debugging: put browser() in a function or run debugonce(f); F10 next line, Shift+F4 step into, Shift+F5 continue, Shift+F8 stop.
r.tip2: Report: in the script, #' lines become text and # %% Title lines start sections; "Build report" collects code, output and plots in a document ready for HTML/PDF.

files.waiting: The working directory appears here once the R session has started.

newVars.title: Create New Variables
newVars.hint: The selected quantities are added to the dataset as one column per case (like Transform > Compute Variable). Nothing is written to a file; save separately if you want to keep it. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
newVars.errStem: Invalid stem (must not end in a digit)
newVars.stemHint: One column per item (e.g. per coefficient, or per model): 1, 2, 3… is appended to the name.
